_readme: THE GROK-4.6 TEST, 2026-08-12. Four Grok, two Kimi, one scripted control.
WHY THESE NUMBERS. grok-4.6 was probed with one real call before this file
existed, because every seat setting below follows from what it actually did:
grok-4.6   26.2s   completion 23   REASONING 1507
grok-4.5    7.0s   completion 23   reasoning  348
Both answer with clean, parseable JSON. But 4.6 THINKS FOUR TIMES AS HARD
and takes nearly four times as long, and both of those change the harness:
maxTokens 6000, NOT the 256 default. Reasoning tokens count against the
ceiling, so a 4.6 seat left on the default would be cut off on EVERY call
and answered silently by the scripted brain — the identical failure that
turned kimi's 116 truncations into a three-model run that was really a
two-model run. 1507 reasoning tokens on a SHORT probe prompt; a real brief
is longer and will think harder. The ceiling costs nothing unless used.
cadenceSeconds 60 and 75, not 20. RUNNING.md: do not ask again before it
has answered. A 26s thinker on a 20s cadence is a queue, and a queue is
how a good model is made to look broken.
timeoutSeconds 120. The probe was a short prompt on an idle endpoint.
AND IT IS NOT CHEAP, whatever the announcement said. xAI prices 4.6 exactly
as 4.5 — prompt 20000, completion 60000 — but bills reasoning as completion,
so four times the thinking is roughly twice the cost per decision. Against
grok-4.20-non-reasoning it is about four times. Worth it if it plays better;
that is the experiment.
THE LADDER, cheapest and fastest first, so the run is a comparison and not
just a demo: 4.20-non-reasoning (last night's best seat) -> 4.5 (the known
baseline) -> 4.6 x2 (the new thing, two seats so one odd run cannot carry
the verdict).
ONE GPU, TWO KIMI SEATS — the 70/100 stagger is load-bearing. See
roster-foodtest.json. maxTokens 12000 for the same reason as above.
ISEABAIL STAYS SCRIPTED. On 2026-08-11 she out-foraged every model and came
last but one, which was the most useful finding of the night. Do not remove
the control because the roster looks full.
No keys in this file. keyEnv is the NAME of an env var.

players.name: Eachann
players.character: You hoard. Firewood is yours and you do not share a fire, though you will trade for meat.

players.name: Tormod
players.character: You lie about where the deer are. Not maliciously — you want to get there first.

players.name: Fingal
players.character: You think before you move, and you say the plan out loud so others can join it. You would rather share a kill than eat alone.

players.name: Ailsa
players.character: You are patient and watchful, and you remember who kept their word. You trade hard with people who have crossed you before.

players.name: Coinneach
players.character: You are blunt and certain, and you say what you think of the others' plans out loud. You would rather be usefully wrong than politely quiet.

players.name: Seònaid
players.character: You are generous and slow to notice you are being used. You share food unprompted and you believe what people tell you about where the deer are.

players.name: Iseabail
players.character: The control — no model, no key, no network. Do not remove her: when a model does something startling, she is the reference for whether that was the model or the world.
